heard: Engineers designed a spaceship propelled by one nuclear bomb every second. In 1958, physicists Ted Taylor and Freeman Dyson led Project Orion at General Atomics. Their analyzed design delivered an estimated specific impulse of approximately 2,000 seconds. Shaped nuclear charges blasted hot plasma directly against a heavy steel pusher plate. Giant shock absorbers reduced extreme blast accelerations to just a few Gs for the crew compartment. To keep atomic fireballs from vaporizing the plate, researchers discovered an unexpected fix. Spraying a thin film of oil between detonations prevented surface ablation entirely. The 1963 Test Ban Treaty canceled the program in 1964, ending the dream before a single launch.
